# Job Chapter 29 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 426v–427r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JOB_029_page_001.jpg, JOB_029_page_002.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** And Job again took up his discourse and said:

**2** "Oh, that I were as in the months of old, as in the days when God watched over me,

**3** when his lamp shone above my head, and by his light I walked through darkness;

**4** as I was in the prime of my days, when the intimate friendship of God was upon my tent;

**5** when the Almighty was yet with me, and my children were around me;

**6** when my steps were bathed in cream, and the rock poured out for me streams of oil!

**7** When I went out to the gate of the city, when I took my seat in the square,

**8** the young men saw me and stepped aside, and the aged rose to their feet.

**9** The princes held back their words and put their hand over their mouths.

**10** The voice of the nobles was hushed, and their tongue clung to the roof of their mouths.

**11** When the ear heard, it blessed me, and when the eye saw, it commended me,

**12** because I delivered the poor who cried for help, and the fatherless who had no one to aid him.

**13** The blessing of the dying came upon me, and I caused the widow's heart to sing for joy.

**14** I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; my justice was like a robe and a turban.

**15** I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame.

**16** I was a father to the needy, and I searched out the case of the stranger.

**17** I broke the jaws of the unrighteous and made him drop his prey from his teeth.

**18** Then I thought, 'I shall die in my own nest, and I shall multiply my days as the sand.

**19** My roots spread out to the waters, and the dew lies all night on my branches.

**20** My glory is ever fresh with me, and my bow is renewed in my hand.'

**21** They listened to me and waited, and kept silence for my counsel.

**22** After I spoke they did not speak again, and my word dropped upon them like dew.

**23** They waited for me as for the rain, and they opened their mouths wide for the spring rain.

**24** I smiled on them when they had no confidence, and the light of my face they did not cast down.

**25** I chose their way and sat as chief, and I lived like a king among his troops, like one who comforts mourners."

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Job 29 is the first panel of a triptych (29-30-31): past glory, present misery, and oath of innocence. This chapter functions as a legal exhibit — Job describes his former life not out of nostalgia but as evidence for his case. The structure moves from divine blessing (vv.2-6) through social honor (vv.7-11) to ethical achievement (vv.12-17) to confident expectation (vv.18-20) and back to social preeminence (vv.21-25). The portrait is of a man who was not merely prosperous but profoundly good — rescuing the poor, defending orphans, serving as eyes to the blind and feet to the lame. This is the life that God blessed and then, seemingly without cause, destroyed. The contrast with chapter 30 is the emotional core of Job's argument.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.4 — "counsel of God" vs. "friendship of God" vs. "intimate friendship"
- **EMET:** "the-counsel [sod] of-God"
- **LOGOS:** "the friendship of God"
- **PNEUMA:** "God's intimate friendship"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "the intimate friendship of God" — *sod* implies both counsel and close companionship. Adding "intimate" captures the warmth of the Hebrew.

### V.18 — "as the sand" (*chol*) vs. "as the phoenix"
- **EMET:** "like-the-sand [ka-chol]" (with note on phoenix reading)
- **LOGOS:** "as the sand" (with note on phoenix)
- **PNEUMA:** "as many days as there are grains of sand"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "as the sand" — the primary meaning of *chol* is "sand." The phoenix reading is fascinating but secondary; it is noted in the EMET and LOGOS apparatus.

### V.24 — "I laughed at them" vs. "I smiled on them"
- **EMET:** "I-laughed [eschaq] at-them — they-did-not believe"
- **LOGOS:** "I smiled on them when they had no confidence"
- **PNEUMA:** "When I smiled at them, they could hardly believe it"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "I smiled on them when they had no confidence" — *sachaq* can mean either "laugh" or "smile." Context favors a warm, encouraging gesture.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
